title: review: C-O9 fix round 1: reconcile_dead resolves a base without goal/<parent>, orphaned results always get a review, requeue clears dispatched_at, tick() survives reconcile errors
spec:
Fix round for T-0130 (branch task/T-0130, commit f3d1f10). Work in this task's worktree, cut from task/T-0130. Review T-0132 (opus) requested changes; items below come from it. Do not widen scope.

1 MED daemon.py reconcile_dead base resolution (≈line 77-86): `task/<id>@{upstream}` never resolves because spawn.ensure_worktree creates branches without --track. When goal/<parent> does not exist (parentless task, or the first execute task of a goal), use `git merge-base HEAD origin/main` in the worktree, and if origin/main is absent too, `git merge-base HEAD main`; only when none resolves fall back to requeue. Test: an execute task with no goal/<parent> branch whose worktree has one commit ahead of main → regated with the commit sha.

2 MED daemon.py gate() (≈line 283): a result with `orphaned: true` must never merge directly, whatever the complexity. In gate(), when `(t.get("result") or {}).get("orphaned")` is truthy, always create the review task (with tier=review_tier(t)) instead of merge.merge, and put "orphaned executor: verify the acceptance criteria are fully met, the worker may have died mid-task" at the start of the review task's spec. Test: complexity 2 execute task with an orphaned done result → after gate, a review task exists with inputs=[id] and no merge happened.

3 MED daemon.py requeue path: every place reconcile_dead (and the old one-liner it replaced) sets status back to "queued" must also clear the pipeline stamp so dispatch() retries: `bus.update(id, status="queued", pid=None, reason=..., pipeline={k: v for k, v in pipeline.items() if k != "dispatched_at"})`. Test: reconcile_dead returns "requeued" and a following tick() with a fake executor (see how existing dispatch tests stub executor.start / spawn_async) dispatches the task again (dispatched_at re-stamped, executor.start called once). Rename or extend test_reconcile_dead_requeues_when_no_commits_ahead accordingly.

4 LOW daemon.py tick(): wrap the reconcile_dead call per task in try/except Exception as e: print(f"[daemon] reconcile {id} failed: {e}", file=sys.stderr) and continue, so a vanished worktree or task file cannot abort the stage loop. Test: a running task with a dead pid whose worktree path does not exist and whose git call is patched to raise → tick() still runs dispatch/gate/merge (assert via a stub stage or that the other tasks progress).

5 LOW tests/test_daemon.py: the new tests must use the real task ids for branch names (task/<tid>) and cover the no-parent case from item 1; keep the existing four cases green.

6 LOW daemon.py dirty check: keep `--porcelain` counting untracked files as dirty and add a one-line comment saying so and why (held is the safe direction). No behaviour change.

No new dependency. Finish with: summary, files changed, failures-only test output. Commit on the task branch when green (git add the two files, git commit) — the previous round's worker forgot to commit, do not.
acceptance: Without goal/<parent>, reconcile_dead uses merge-base against origin/main or main and regates a clean worktree with commits ahead (test)
gate() never merges a result carrying orphaned true directly; it creates a review task at review_tier(t) whose spec starts with the orphaned warning (test at complexity 2)
Every requeue path drops pipeline.dispatched_at and the next tick dispatches the task again (test with stubbed executor.start)
tick() wraps reconcile_dead per task; an exception there does not prevent dispatch/gate/merge_reviewed from running (test)
New tests use task/<real id> branch names and cover the no-parent case; existing tests green; dirty-check comment added
uv run python -m unittest discover -q tests green; no new dependency; only daemon.py and tests/test_daemon.py change; work is committed on task/<this id>
